synthesis.body: When adding a uniqueness check to an existing corpus, read the index for improvised notation before assuming the corpus is clean. A project that has been living with a violation has usually already invented a local workaround, and that workaround is what the new check trips over. One repository carried three different workarounds for the same class of violation: a suffixed identifier form the conventions define nowhere, two rows carrying the same identifier with a prose note asserting the rule did not apply, and an index that simply dropped a row so the second member had no entry at all. The control consequence is that a row-internal consistency check could never find the duplicated-identifier case, because those rows agreed with their own targets and disagreed only with each other. Row-internal consistency and one-record-per-identifier are different controls, and the silently dropped row is the failure mode that leaves nothing to search for.

title: A corpus living with a violation has already invented a workaround — read the index before adding the check
